findings.fix: Remove Company website, Membership number, Account number and Organization name from account creation, or make them optional and collect them only where the account actually uses them (for example a separate business-account flow).

instances.evidence: <input id="member-input" name="membership_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">

findings.violation: The form's task, named by its heading Set up your account and its submit label Create account, is creating a new personal shopping account, which that task cannot use a company website for, and the field is required, so nobody can create the account without supplying one.

findings.fix: Say beside the field what the number is used for, or make it optional.
findings.violation: A phone number is required with no word beside the field on why it is needed, though the form already asks for an email address.

findings.fix: Move the rule into hint text beside the field, linked with aria-describedby.
findings.violation: A format rule appears only in the placeholder, which disappears as soon as typing starts.

findings.fix: Mark the optional fields with the word optional in their labels, or mark the required ones and explain the mark.

findings.violation: The form mixes 14 required and 1 optional fields and marks none of them, so the person cannot tell which may be left empty.
A control that clears everything entered sits directly beside the submit button.

findings.fix: Remove the font-size and padding overrides, or raise them so the rendered control is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
findings.violation: The declared style sets an 11-pixel font with 1 to 2 pixels of padding, which renders a button well under 20 CSS pixels tall, far below the roughly 44-pixel target mobile-usability guidance recommends and a size a fingertip can miss on the first tap.

findings.evidence: <button id="submit-btn" type="submit">Create account</button> <button id="reset-btn" type="reset">Clear form</button>
findings.fix: Style the primary submit as the visually dominant control (for example a filled, higher-contrast button) and render Clear form as a visibly lesser, secondary-styled control, or remove it.
findings.violation: The document declares no stylesheet or style attribute on either button, so the primary action, Create account, and the destructive Clear form action render in the identical default button style with no difference in prominence, and a person must read both labels to tell which one saves their entry.

findings.evidence: <input id="name-input" name="full_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" required> (line 12) ... <input id="given-input" name="given_name" type="text" autocomplete="given-name" required> <input id="family-input" name="family_name" type="text" autocomplete="family-name" required> (lines 61, 63)
findings.fix: Collect the name once: keep either the single Full name field or the First/Last name pair, not both.
findings.violation: The form already asked for the person's name once, as a single required Full name field (#name-input, line 12), then asks for it again later as two more required fields, First name (#given-input, line 61) and Last name (#family-input, line 63), so the person must re-type their name and cannot tell which of the two asks the account actually uses.

findings.evidence: <select id="shipspeed-select" required> <option>Standard</option> <option>Express</option> <option>Overnight</option> </select> (line 53) ... <input id="contacttime-input" name="contact_time" type="text" required=""> (line 71)
findings.fix: Drop these two fields from account creation and ask for shipping speed at checkout and contact time when a contact is actually scheduled.
findings.violation: Preferred shipping speed (#shipspeed-select, line 53) and Preferred contact time (#contacttime-input, line 71) both answer questions that only matter once there is an order to ship or a reason to call, not while creating an account, so creating the account forces an answer to a question the task could ask later instead.
This account number is a text field without the numeric input mode, so a phone shows the full keyboard for digits.

findings.fix: Offer the options as visible radio buttons.
findings.violation: A single choice among 3 options sits in a drop-down, so the person must open it to see them.
